subject: Private Offer: AWS Marketplace Rev-Share & Term Alignment for AcmeApps
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Samira Khan <samira@acmeapps.com>, Marc Jensen <mjensen@amazon.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer draft submitted to AWS — AcmeApps (rev-share ask)

Team — looping you on the private offer we negotiated with AcmeApps. Key points from the customer and AWS Marketplace pre-review: 

- List price: $0.60/token-equivalent (workload estimate attached)
- Customer requested 25% discount off list for first 12 months (marketing-led onboarding incentive)
- AWS Marketplace private offer requires rev-share 20% to AWS; AcmeApps is asking for a custom rev-share carveout of 10% for the first year to preserve their margins
- Term: 12 months with auto-renew; AcmeApps wants 6-month early termination for convenience

Attached: Acme_Private_Offer_Draft.pdf and AWS_PO_TermSheet.xlsx — AWS pre-review flagged the non-standard rev-share request and the 6-month termination clause as items that need Redwood exec approval prior to Marketplace publication.

Ask: Can we approve an exception to the standard rev-share alignment (i.e., allow a 10% rev-share to AWS for year 1, with Redwood covering the 10% delta via a marketing credit) and accept a modified termination clause? If not, we need a clear fallback position to communicate to the customer by EOD tomorrow.

Context: Acme is a mid-market ISV with a committed upsell path; this private offer is strategic for our Marketplace channel expansion. Deal: RW-ACME-2026-03.

[Attachment: Acme_Private_Offer_Draft.pdf (PDF, 124 KB)]
[Attachment: AWS_PO_TermSheet.xlsx (XLSX, 42 KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 11:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer draft submitted to AWS — AcmeApps (rev-share ask)

Thanks, Sergio. Quick read-through: 

- I agree this is strategically important for the Marketplace play and likely worth some short-term margin tradeoff, but we need finance and legal sign-off before granting non-standard economics or termination terms.
- Vivek: please confirm whether we can absorb a 10% rev-share credit in Q2 without breaking GAAP recognition expectations or impacting reported ARR targets for the quarter. If there's a way to structure as a marketing credit vs. price reduction that preserves recognition, call it out.
- Laura: please review the 6-month termination ask — specifically the downstream indemnity and data/PII obligations if the agreement terminates early. Also flag any AWS-specific contract language that Amazon will insist on in the private offer.

Rishi: if finance/legal can greenlight with concrete guardrails, I will take this to execs for final approval (I can route a short memo outlining the ask + impact). If either group pushes back, prepare the fallback: either (A) keep standard 20% rev-share and offer a one-time onboarding credit from Redwood, or (B) shorten the term to 6 months with pro-rated pricing and standard rev-share.

--Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

Thanks for the context. I reviewed the draft and have the following high-level redlines and considerations: 

1) Termination: a 6-month unilateral convenience termination by the customer creates revenue leakage and operational risk. If we accept, require a 30-day cure period for material breaches and a pro-rata refund schedule tied to usage and pre-paid credits. No early termination without cause should wipe out obligations around data retention and security audits.

2) Rev-share/credits: Structuring the 10% difference as a marketing credit (paid by Redwood) rather than a list price reduction is preferable from a commercial wording perspective. However, we must explicitly document that the credit is non-refundable and only applies to AWS private offer consumption to avoid downstream resale/aggregation exposure.

3) AWS contract clauses: AWS will likely require flow-down clauses for certain security and export controls; confirm whether we will accept AWS indemnity carve-outs. If we intend to reimburse AWS marketing credits, we need a clear expense recognition path.

4) Data residency & audit: If Acme requests SOC2 evidence or dedicated logging for Marketplace transactions, we should limit the scope to access logs and denial-of-service metrics; avoid full tenant-level exports unless they sign a higher-tier support/engagement.

Please see attached legal redline (Legal_redline_Acme.docx). I can draft the short exec memo Marissa referenced if you want me to summarize the legal risk and proposed mitigations.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer draft submitted to AWS — AcmeApps (rev-share ask)

Marissa / team — I reviewed the numbers and the accounting implications. Summary: 

- We can accommodate a Redwood-funded marketing credit equivalent to the 10% rev-share delta for year 1, provided we structure it as a contra-revenue marketing expense recognized over the 12-month term. That preserves ARR recognition but will reduce gross margin in Q2.
- We cannot treat the credit as a price reduction if the customer intends to claim that net price for resale analytics; it must be a separate line item in the PO/Invoice.
- Early termination risk: if the customer exercises 6-month convenience termination, we will need an accelerated reconciliation clause to recover any unused marketing credit. Finance can support a pro-rata clawback mechanism in the private offer paperwork.

If legal signs off on the wording Laura proposed and the clawback language, finance will greenlight the economics. Recommend we present a 2-option memo to execs: 
A) Approve 10%-to-AWS rev-share carveout funded by Redwood marketing credit with legal guardrails and a pro-rata clawback on termination. Expected FY impact: ~-$120k marketing expense in 2026 Q2 (estimate).
B) Decline custom rev-share; offer an onboarding credit up-front (one-time) of up to $75k and keep standard 20% rev-share.

I'll attach a short P&L snapshot if helpful. Timebox: need exec decision by EOD 3/12 to meet AWS private offer publication timeline.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Finance | Redwood Inference

Subject: Exec approval requested: AcmeApps AWS Private Offer (rev-share & term exceptions)

All — thanks for the fast turnaround. Per legal/finance input, we have a recommended path that balances GTM velocity with risk controls. I am escalating to the exec committee for a quick decision: approve Option A outlined below or select Option B. Need a yes/no from execs by 5pm PT today to meet AWS publication window.

Option A (recommended):
- Approve Redwood-funded marketing credit to cover the 10% rev-share delta for 12 months (credit paid as contra-revenue, pro-rata, with clawback on early termination).
- Accept 12-month term with auto-renew; allow customer 6-month convenience termination only if they reimburse unused portion of the marketing credit on a pro-rata basis.
- Legal to finalize wording: non-refundable credit, limited to AWS private offer consumption; flow-down clauses for AWS accepted per legal redline.

Projected impact: ~$120k marketing expense in 2026 Q2; expected ARR uplift $720k ARR in year 1 (conservative). Strategic upside: unlocks marketplace co-sell motion and provides joint-marketing runway with AWS.

Option B (fallback):
- Decline rev-share carveout. Keep standard AWS rev-share at 20%. Offer a one-time onboarding credit up to $75k (non-recurring), no special termination rights.

Please reply-all with APPROVE A or APPROVE B. If no response by 17:00 PT, we will default to Option B and inform Acme and AWS.

Thanks — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Global Sales | Redwood Inference
